results.prompt: Explain the difference between RAM and SSD to a non-technical person.
results.response:
RAM, or Random Access Memory, is like your short term memory in our brains; it's where all currently open applications run at once while you work on different tasks simultaneously. It lets computers access data quickly because the information doesn't have to be read from a physical location - instead, everything is stored right there inside RAM for immediate use by the computer. But just like we forget things if they aren't frequently used in our minds, RAM also has its limitations and gets cleared when your laptop or computer goes into sleep mode or is turned off.

On the other hand, an SSD (Solid State Drive) works more like a library where books are stored on shelves for later use. These drives store data even after you shut down your device because they keep everything written onto them permanently - this includes all saved documents, pictures and applications which can be accessed quickly from the storage drive when needed again in future without any loss of information due to power cuts or system crashes like sometimes happens with RAM. However, retrieving these files is a bit slower compared to using your immediate memory (RAM) because it takes longer time for data stored on SSD shelves (hard drives) to be found and read out when needed again at some point in the future by your computer's brain!

In summary - RAM helps computers run multiple applications simultaneously while working right now, but needs constant supply of power or else its contents get lost just like forgetting things over time. SSD is a more reliable storage option for long term use where data remains safe even after shutdown with slower access times when compared to using immediate memory (RAM).
